subject: CSA assertion index + runtime log snapshot for Shoreline Bank scope
messages:
From: Jane Ortega <jane.ortega@shorelinebank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CSA control mapping + sample runtime logs (Shoreline scope)

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick intro. Shoreline is kicking off a CSA review for the services that will be in scope for our vaulting and payments pilot (API endpoints, embeddings, and model inference on dedicated pools). We need a control-by-control assertion package mapped to the CSA/CAIQ matrix and a small set of runtime artifacts so our auditors can validate operational behavior. Specifically, could you provide: 

- A control index (CSA control id -> Redwood assertion -> evidence artifacts) for the scoped components (networking, tenant isolation, key management, logging/telemetry, change control)
- A redacted runtime log sample (token routing / request headers / model variant routing) that demonstrates tenant routing and KV cache hits for a short window (no customer data, redacted IDs ok)
- A short snippet or runbook showing tenant isolation checks and the keystore rotation schedule/proof

Timeline: auditor asked for an initial package by 2028-06-30. If you can’t meet that, please suggest the earliest realistic delivery date.

Also happy to do a 30-min walkthrough once you have the package to help the auditor interpret artifacts.

Jane Ortega
Security Assessments, Shoreline Bank
jane.ortega@shorelinebank.com

--
Note: please send documents to the secure intake link or encrypted attachment. We flagged HS-19342 as the audit ticket for tracking.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Ortega <jane.ortega@shorelinebank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CSA control mapping + sample runtime logs (Shoreline scope)

Jane — thanks for the clear ask and the HS ticket. We'll take this on. Internal owners below; I copied them so we have a single place for questions.

High-level plan:
- Kimberly: prepare the CSA control index mapping (spreadsheet) and assertions
- Marissa: gather the runtime log sample and tenant-isolation snippet; she will sanitize/redact and provide a short narrative for the auditor
- David: provide the key rotation schedule and cryptographic control references (KMS/HSM attestations)

We aim to deliver an initial bundle by 2028-06-29 EOD to give you 1 day for review — target meets your 6/30 ask. If we see blockers we'll surface immediately.

Would you prefer the artifacts uploaded to your secure intake link (you referenced) or a Google Drive share with restricted access? Also, can we schedule a 30-min walkthrough on Tue 6/27 or Thu 6/29?

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Security & Controls, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Subject: CSA assertion index + attached artifacts (initial)

Marcus / Marissa — attaching the first pass of the CSA control index. I compiled per-control assertions for the scoped services and added an evidence column that points to artifacts we can produce. Attachments included: redwood_csa_assertions_v1.xlsx and a redacted runtime log sample (runtime_log_sample_20280620.json).

Notes on the spreadsheet:
- Tab 1 (Index): control id, short assertion, owner, evidence filename(s)
- Tab 2 (Evidence pointers): links and descriptions (where we will surface things like KMS rotation, AMI/image build proofs, RBAC screenshots)
- Tab 3 (Exclusions): controls out of scope for this pilot (with rationale)

About the runtime log sample: I included a 30-second window showing two routed requests, KV-cache hit counts, and region routing. We redacted request identifiers and replaced tenant IDs with placeholders (TENANT_RED_1). The runtime snippet is intentionally small and annotated in a separate sheet in the workbook; also exported the same sample as a JSON attachment per Jane's preference.

I will follow up with the tenant isolation snippet and the KMS rotation doc (David is pulling the rotation proof).

Kimberly Park
Director, Controls & Compliance
redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_csa_assertions_v1.xlsx, runtime_log_sample_20280620.json

Thanks Kimberly — this looks helpful. A couple quick asks before the walkthrough: 

- Can you confirm whether the runtime sample shows (a) KV cache hits vs misses, and (b) which model variant served each request? The auditor will want to see clear linkage between request metadata and routing decisions.
- For the tenant isolation snippet: are those checks automated at request time or performed as part of the deployment pipeline? A short sentence will suffice in the narrative.

We'd like to set the walkthrough for Thu 2028-06-29 at 10:00 AM PT if that works for your team; please send a calendar invite.

Jane Ortega

Jane / team —

Thanks — Thu 2028-06-29 10:00 AM PT works for us. Calendar invite sent. Quick clarifications ahead of the call:

- Runtime sample: Marissa confirmed the exported sample contains explicit KV cache hit/miss counters and a model_variant field for each routed request. We will open the sample in the walkthrough and show the mapping in the spreadsheet (Index -> evidence filename -> annotated line numbers).
- Tenant isolation: checks are enforced at request-time by the routing layer (automated) and verified during CI/CD gate tests; the tenant_isolation_snippet.txt we'll surface shows the runtime check plus the CI job name and log excerpt.
- Key rotation: David attached the rotation schedule as a separate secure artifact to the intake ticket (KMS rotation proof, key ID mapping).

Next steps: Kimberly will upload the final index and annotated artifacts to the secure intake link (or Drive if you prefer) by EOD today; Marissa will prepare a 3-slide walkthrough deck for the call. If you want the artifacts earlier, let us know and we can push them now.

—Marcus
